SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 2-3 day history of constant dull ache below the umbilicus associated with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.
- Associated symptoms: ↑ urinary frequency without dysuria/urgency/odor; mild pink discoloration noted in urine over last 2 days (patient unsure if menstrual spotting); no vomiting; no diarrhea; constipation one week ago now resolved; no vaginal discharge; no light-headedness.
- Onset/progression: Gradual onset over past 2 days; symptoms persisting.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period ≈ 3 + weeks ago; expects menses soon; sexually active with one partner; etonogestrel implant (Implanon) in situ; uncertain pregnancy status.
- Past medical history: None reported.
- Past surgical history: Not discussed.
- Medications: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented; no other regular medications.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).
- Social history: Non-smoker; lives with boyfriend; no alcohol/drug use discussed.
- Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed in video consult; no vitals available.
- No investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with nausea
   - Assessment: Undifferentiated lower abdominal pain; rule out early pregnancy and genitourinary causes.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early pregnancy/ectopic pregnancy, urinary tract infection, constipation/functional bowel pain, pelvic inflammatory disease, dysmenorrhea.
   - Investigations planned: Urine pregnancy test; urinalysis ± culture; physical abdominal and pelvic examination; consider β-hCG, FBC, CRP, pelvic ultrasound if indicated.
   - Treatment planned: To be determined after in-person assessment.
   - Referral: Same-day face-to-face GP review arranged.

2. Possible urinary symptoms/hematuria
   - Assessment: Increased frequency with pink tinge; etiology unclear (menstrual spotting vs microscopic hematuria).
   - Differential diagnosis: Urinary tract infection, menstruation, urethral irritation, renal calculi (low likelihood).
   - Investigations planned: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture during in-person visit.

3. Medication allergy documentation
   - Assessment: Amoxicillin allergy noted.
   - Plan: Flag in medical record; avoid prescribing penicillins.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements:
  - No vital signs or physical examination documented; will be obtained at in-person visit.
  - Reaction details for amoxicillin allergy not specified.
  - Medication reconciliation incomplete (OTC/vitamins not discussed).
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor conversational overlaps but key clinical information intelligible.
